Which DHCP option, when required, should be configured and enabled to help APs locate their wireless LAN controller?
C
DHCP Option 43 carries vendor-specific discovery information that compatible APs can use to learn the WLAN controller's IP address.

When deploying a new WLAN infrastructure using PoE to power the APs, you realize that a known good AP is not powering up. You use the same cable to connect your laptop and connect without any trouble. What is the most likely reason the AP did not power up?
Missing AP licenses in the controller
Spanning-tree convergence
Layer 3 routing
Lack of PoE budget on the switch
D
PoE planning must use the maximum power the switch can supply per port and multiply it by the number of powered APs, while keeping the total within the switch's available budget.
During your first pre-deployment meeting with the deployment team, you hand out the full design documentation to all of them. What's your primary goal during this meeting?
To explain design decisions and ensure understanding of design documents.
To discuss AP functionality.
To explain how Wi-Fi works.
To justify the budget.
A
The kickoff meeting aligns installers with the design intent. Explaining the design decisions helps prevent field changes that undermine RF performance.
A controller-based WLAN infrastructure has its controller on a different subnet than its APs. What device must be used to enable any communication between the Controller and the APs?
NTP server
Router
PoE Layer 2 switch
Wireless bridge
B
A router provides Layer 3 connectivity between different IP subnets so APs can reach a controller outside their local subnet.
In what circumstance would you not enable DFS channels on a WLAN infrastructure?
In any stadium
In any office complex
In an airport
In any home office
C
Channels 116–124 are DFS channels in the 5 GHz band. Radar detection can force channel changes, which may disrupt real-time voice clients.
Aesthetics are very important in some environments. What common installation technique can be used to best meet this requirement in a stadium?
Painting to match team colors
Using enclosures under the seats or on hand-rails
Mounting on a non-fixed pole
Mounting on the walls
B

Under-seat or handrail enclosures conceal APs in a stadium while maintaining a practical mounting position. Use an approved enclosure so the installation does not compromise RF performance or warranty.
What kind of site survey helps you identify if roaming is working as designed?
Passive
Predictive
Active
Spectrum analysis walkthrough
C
An active survey associates and exchanges traffic while the client moves. It is therefore suitable for observing whether roaming succeeds and whether sessions remain usable.

When doing some frame capturing over the air during a voice call, you realized that frames on the downlink (from the AP to the client) direction are not being transmitted with the correct UP value for voice frames, but on the uplink (from the client to the AP) direction are being transmitted correctly. What's the cause of this issue?
Bad client driver
AP is not receiving enough PoE, thus not using QoS features
Somewhere on the wired network QoS markings aren't being trusted
Faulty antenna on the AP
C

The wired network must preserve and trust the QoS/DSCP markings used to classify voice traffic. If a switch or router resets or ignores those markings, the AP may map the downlink frames to the wrong 802.11 User Priority.

You are validating association capabilities from clients to an 802.1X/EAP secure SSID. The RADIUS server's IP address is 10.100.50.25 and the default RADIUS authentication port is used. When testing them, none of the clients are able to associate to the SSID. Troubleshooting the WLAN infrastructure, you found out that the server is up and the RADIUS service is up as well, but the authenticator is not able to communicate properly with the server. What's your next troubleshooting step?
Verify that the shared secret between the authenticator and the RADIUS server is correct
Reboot the clients
Reboot the server
Restart the RADIUS service
A
The RADIUS shared secret must match on the authenticator and server; a mismatch prevents valid RADIUS messages from being accepted.
During lunch time in the break room of a company, Wi-Fi connectivity on the 2.4 GHz band is intermittent. Every other time of the day, it works fine. What's the likely cause of this issue?
Employees are using their cell data instead of using the Wi-Fi
The AP in the cafeteria keeps rebooting due to lack of PoE budget on the switch
Toasters and ovens are heating up the air, raising the noise floor with the Wi-Fi on the 2.4 Ghz band
Microwaves in the cafeteria are interfering with the Wi-Fi on the 2.4 GHz band
D
Microwave ovens can emit energy in the 2.4 GHz band while operating, raising interference and causing intermittent Wi-Fi performance nearby.

After deploying a 5 GHz-only WLAN infrastructure in the USA, using 20 MHz channel-widths and all 25 available channels, one of the managers of the company brings his 802.11n tablet to the office to test the Guest SSID. While testing, there were several spots where we would get poor RSSI (below -80dBM) or none at all. You checked the WLAN infrastructure and all APs are up and running and you've validated coverage after deployment. What is causing this issue?
His tablet doesn't support the 5 GHz band
His tablet only supports a 40 MHz channel-width
His tablet does not support one or more of the 5 GHz channels
His tablet doesn't support MU-MIMO
D

The supplied key selects MU-MIMO, but MU-MIMO is a capacity feature and does not itself determine RSSI. The scenario's symptom may instead point to channel compatibility; verify this item against the source before using it for scoring.

After designing and deploying a WLAN infrastructure, you realized the CCI is causing poor performance in the 2.4 GHz band. Primarily, you've designed the WLAN for 5 GHz and 2.4 GHz as a best effort. You found out that the implementers didn't follow your guidelines when configuring the WLAN infrastructure. What can you do to minimize as much as possible the CCI impact in the 2.4 GHz band?
Add more APs to the infrastructure
Increase the transmit power on all APs
Turn-off 2.4 GHz radios on some APs
Use all channels available in the 2.4 GHz band
C
Turning off selected 2.4 GHz radios reduces same-channel reuse and contention. It can improve performance without introducing adjacent-channel overlap.

You have performed a validation site survey after deploying a WLAN infrastructure that is an All- Wireless-Office. One specific application of your customer is experiencing delay when using the application after moving from wired connectivity. After your validation, you realized that all APs are using 80 MHz channel-widths instead of 20 MHz on the 5 GHz band, as it was designed. What can be done to resolve the delay on this application?
APs should be using 160 MHz channel-widths to get more throughput
Reconfigure to use 20 MHz channel-widths, so reuse of the frequency is more effective
Power-off half of the APs to reduce CCI and keep 80 MHz channel-widths
Add more APs using 80 MHz channel-widths
B
Narrower channels provide more opportunities for channel reuse and reduce the number of APs competing on the same spectrum, often improving capacity in dense WLANs.
What are the deliverables to your customer after successfully implementing a WLAN infrastructure?
Digital or physical assets, guides, floorplans and configuration documents
Project Charter
Facility blueprints
Nothing is required. The implemented WLAN was deliverable
A
The customer needs the as-built records, configuration documents, floor plans, guides, and transferred assets to operate and support the deployed WLAN.
Who should be in the final meeting from the customer-side after successfully implementing a WLAN infrastructure?
CEO or CFO
End-users
The customer's customers
Remote workers
B

The source answer identifies end users for the final meeting. Their feedback can confirm that the deployed WLAN meets day-to-day usability needs; project acceptance should also involve the sponsor and stakeholders.

During a validation site survey, you realize that the installers mounted some of the APs above the ceiling. They said that this was a request from the building architect due to aesthetics constraints. During the requirements gathering, you weren't advised about any aesthetics constraints from the main stakeholder of the project. What should you do in this case?
Advise the stakeholder that WLAN performance requirements will not be met and a new design process will be needed to meet the requirements.
Leave it as it is and allow automatic channel management to correct any issues.
Increase the output power on all APs by 6 dB immediately.
Remove all external antennas and use only the internal antennas to reduce multipath.
A

Mounting APs above the ceiling changes the propagation environment and adds attenuation not included in the design. Explain the performance impact to the stakeholder and revisit the design rather than simply increasing power.

While performing a validation site survey, you realize that overlapping channels are being used on the 2.4 GHz bad due to the automatic channel assignment algorithm of the WLAN infrastructure. What should you do to prevent this?
Reconfigure the automatic channel assignment settings to use only channels 1, 6, and 11
Purchase and deploy new APs from a different vendor
Reconfigure the network to use static channel plans because automatic channel assignment algorithms are all broken
Leave it as it is; sometimes using all 11 channels in 2.4 GHz gives the optimum performance result
A
In the 2.4 GHz band, channels 1, 6, and 11 are the conventional non-overlapping 20/22 MHz channel plan in North America.

In a convention center, you have received complaints about the WLAN infrastructure. At this moment, there are only two APs in one auditorium. After analyzing the situation, you determined that there are more client devices that the infrastructure was designed for. There are only two APs to support more than 300 devices using the Wi-Fi at the same time. What should you do to make the Wi-Fi work as expected?
Redesign the entire WLAN
Quickly add more APs
Upgrade the Ethernet connections to MultiGig
Turn up the output power on the APs so that they can handle more clients
A
When user density exceeds the original design assumptions, redesign capacity for the actual client count and application demand rather than simply turning up AP power.
What might limit the ability to locate 802.11 clients using a WLAN infrastructure without an 802.11 tag?(Choose all that apply.)
Lack of 802.11k support
When its radio is disabled
When it is off
RF channel selection
B
C
Infrastructure-based location depends on hearing client transmissions. If a device's radio is disabled or the device is powered off, APs cannot receive its Wi-Fi signals to locate it.

While performing a validation site survey, you realize that overlapping channels are being used on the 2.4 GHz bad due to the automatic channel assignment algorithm of the WLAN infrastructure. What should you do to prevent this?
Reconfigure the network to use static channel plans because automatic channel assignment algorithms are all broken
Purchase and deploy new APs from a different vendor
Reconfigure the automatic channel assignment settings to use only channels 1, 6, and 11
Leave it as it is; sometimes using all 11 channels in 2.4 GHz gives the optimum performance result
C
In the 2.4 GHz band, channels 1, 6, and 11 are the conventional non-overlapping 20/22 MHz channel plan in North America.
